- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.4) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to align with sentiment momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or negative; apply a 0.5–1.0% upward bias for first 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day forecasts; if forecast is >1.5σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and price is falling, model often fails to recognize reversal; adjust downward by 0.5–1.0% for next 3–5 days to reflect sentiment decay.
